The numbers are published as FUSE leaves (files under /model/<id>/attention/) and as a stderr summary.

Verdict: approve with nits. No finding shows a wrong number, a crash or a race in production. 7 should-fix items remain:
- 4 CI (continuous integration, the automatic test run on each push) test gaps at production hook call sites
- 1 test that asserts an implementation detail
- 1 PR body whose performance and instruction-count claims were measured ten commits before HEAD
- 1 missing sample count for the T3 (worker-0 job wall) timer /

The head's four unit-test binaries were built and run on this host (claude-box, no AMX unit, no FPGA) with the switch unset, set to 1 and set to yes. All 12 runs (4 binaries x 3 settings) passed. The author's posted runtron numbers are consistent with the code at HEAD.
overview.findings_intro:
Findings are grouped into nine themes and, inside each theme, ordered by severity (should_fix, then nit, then info). Severity means here: should_fix = wrong under a reachable but uncommon condition, or a test that cannot fail on a real break, or a claim in the PR text that is not true of HEAD. nit = wording, style or a one-line hardening. info = a design fact written down for the reader, with no change asked. No must_fix item exists.
Every file:line comes from the earlier stages' grep (the text search tool) at HEAD 04da001cb5.
The three rejected findings (R1-M23, R1-M51, R2-M14) are listed in report-base.json with their rejection reasons. They are not repeated here.

themes_summary.theme: A. Production hook call sites that no CI (continuous integration) test drives
themes_summary.one_line: The hooks are asserted in isolation. The real callers (model::state::forward class rule and token-job count, the per-visit path-bit write at self_attention.hpp:1652, run_attention_job's T2/T3/T4 calls, note_fpga_pass in prepare_uniform_hw_attention) run in no test with the switch on. So a wrong class, a wrong histogram or a swapped busy/wall pair would pass CI. Counts: 4 should_fix, 6 nit, 3 info.

themes_summary.theme: B. Test policy and test hygiene
themes_summary.one_line: One case asserts on raw-hook behavior that is not a contract (against AGENTS.md). One case is framed as a regression test for a same-PR mistake. The rest are literal-vs-named-value mixing, WARN-instead-of-FAIL (the test prints a warning instead of failing) on one-worker pools, key-order substring asserts, a root-uid (user id 0) abort in FUSE cases and a stale CMake (the build configuration tool) comment. Counts: 1 should_fix, 12 nit, 2 info.

themes_summary.theme: C. PR body and posted comments older than HEAD
themes_summary.one_line: The A/A table (base and head timed with the switch off, two arms that are expected to match), objdump (the binary disassembly tool) counts, T1 site, T5 definition, leaf samples, test-case count (12 vs 19) and the 'two arguments' claim describe earlier commits. The 2026-09-30 comment calls a bff317e0d3 run 'the head'. The numbers themselves hold. Counts: 1 should_fix, 12 nit.

T3 has no sample count. So its per-job mean is not derivable when the worker split or the minibatch count (the number of slices a forward's token jobs are processed in) varies. T4 is keyed by operation change and filed under the last layer. T2 contains an output-channel barrier wait. T5 also covers a peer's unpack. rdtsc (the CPU instruction that reads the time-stamp counter) is non-serializing (the CPU may run it before earlier instructions finish). Counts: 1 should_fix, 7 nit, 1 info.

Undefined or stale words in README.stats.md and the header Notes: 'visit', 'worker 0' vs pool worker, active_workers, fpga_queries, the off-state leaf rule, the transient forwards-ahead-by-one read window, the exception-unwind claim on a noexcept function. Counts: 18 nit.

themes_summary.theme: F. Lifetime, FUSE and concurrency edges
themes_summary.one_line: Reachable but uncommon conditions with a documented or one-line remedy: two live states sharing one model id, a leaf read across state destruction, a two-call FUSE read of a growing leaf, relaxed-store ordering of n_attn_workers_min, an unescaped model_id in the stderr report, a scheduler invariant no assert checks. Counts: 11 nit, 6 info.

themes_summary.theme: G. Off-state cost and code placement
themes_summary.one_line: Small costs paid with the switch unset (a byte store per visit, a 64-byte tally zeroed per call, no tron_unlikely hint (the macro that tells the compiler a branch is rarely taken), three pool-worker formulas). The A/A measurement in the PR body bounds them below its resolution of 0.5 to 0.7 % (the run-to-run spread of that measurement). Counts: 2 nit, 4 info.

Literals 0/1/true/false and repeated strings where the guide asks for named values, constants without value suffixes, brace-less multi-line loops, include hygiene, redundant inline, constant-zero keys. Counts: 8 nit.

themes_summary.theme: I. Design facts, accepted as designed
themes_summary.one_line: Recorded for the reader, no change asked: fpga_query_passes counts logical passes, a zero-job forward would be decode_like (unreachable today), n_layers follows plugin::n_layers, mixed forwards file other users' decode attention under prompt_or_mixed. Counts: 4 info.

counters.intro:
Short version. Every exported counter and timer of PR 4596 at HEAD 04da001cb5 was traced from its writer to its FUSE key. Fourteen of the nineteen rows count what they claim with no reachable omission or double count. The open items are test gaps (the forward-level counters, the path-set histogram, the run_attention_job timer hooks and the FPGA hooks run in no test with the switch on), one design gap (T3 has no sample count), and documentation mismatches.

Words used here. / Counter = an atomic uint64 in attn_stats.hpp read by a FUSE leaf. / Visit = one apply_page_tok call (one query slice against one KV page for one KV head). / k_tokens = K tokens scored per KV head. / Cycles = TSC ticks (tsc_hz in the summary leaf converts them to seconds). / Row = worker_layer_row keyed by (forward class, pool worker, layer) [attn_stats.hpp:392]. / Class = decode_like or prompt_or_mixed, chosen once per forward [model.hpp:1668-1672]. / Pool worker of attention worker i = n_workers (the number of threads in the pool) - n_attn_workers + i [attn_stats.hpp:431-435].

Common facts for every row. Initialization: model_stats constructor allocates rows, fpga, timers and path_bits only when enabled [attn_stats.hpp:376-380]. Every counter starts at 0 except n_attn_workers_min, which starts at UINT64_MAX [attn_stats.hpp:300]. / Reset: none. Counters accumulate over the life of the model state and are never reset [attn_stats.hpp:71]. An interval is the difference of two reads. Per-forward scratch only is reset: fpga_bits reassigned [attn_stats.hpp:455], path_bits cleared after the fold (the end_forward step that combines the per-worker path bits of each token job) [attn_stats.hpp:570], T4 state reset [attn_stats.hpp:459-460]. / Destruction prints the stderr report [attn_stats.hpp:388-390]. / Aggregation: sum_layer sums all pool-worker rows of one layer and adds the layer timers [attn_stats.hpp:651-658]. sum_worker sums the layers of one worker [attn_stats.hpp:660-665]. render_totals sums the layers [attn_stats.hpp:739-756]. put_counts prints the keys [attn_stats.hpp:672-695]. put_fpga prints the FPGA keys [attn_stats.hpp:699-704]. / Every file:line below was checked with sed -n on the read-only worktree (a git checkout directory) at HEAD 04da001cb5.

The served path is set at exactly three return sites: amx for a dense 64-token page (a page whose 64 tokens form one range) [self_attention.hpp:1898], empty when no token of the page is scored [self_attention.hpp:1950], avx otherwise [self_attention.hpp:1982]. The pass index comes from run_sections' pending flag [self_attention.hpp:1684]. Each visit is counted once per KV head, as the README says.

No reachable omission or double count. Every (query, page) pair lies in exactly one section (existing assertion, t_llama_unit.cpp:2660-2698). A call that dismissed every page adds nothing (n_visits == 0 [attn_stats.hpp:483]).
Test gaps: no test drives an empty visit through apply_page_range with stats on (R1-M25). FPGA-layer software-mix tallies are not asserted in CI (continuous integration, the automated test runs) (R1-M35).
Documentation gaps: the kill-switch identity in the PR body uses ready+pending sums that no leaf prints (R2-M17). README never defines visit or the ready/pending split (R1-M21).

conditions.intro:
Conditions table for tron PR #4596 (attention path stats behind the environment switch TRON_ATTN_STATS) at HEAD 04da001cb5, diff base 66c7bb8db1. Rows come from lens-coverage.json (19 lenses, where a lens is one review pass over the code for one named topic). Every file:line in the evidence column is a line a lens named as read at HEAD, plus lines I re-read with sed -n at HEAD (self_attention.hpp:485-488 and 1274-1284, model.hpp:1668-1672, full.hpp:1999-2005, CMakeLists.txt:48, llama.hpp:751-753, TronCpp.hs:1317-1319). A grep of .github, ci, flake.nix and t/CMakeLists.txt for TRON_ATTN_STATS returned nothing.  / Status meanings: / - checked_by_reading = a lens read the named lines and reached a conclusion. A test or run may exist in addition, and it is then named in the evidence. / - test_run_needed = only a build or a machine run can settle the item. / - not_checked = no lens read the relevant code.  / Host limits: the unit tests of the head were built and run on this host (claude-box, an AMD Zen 5 machine) with TRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON. All 12 runs passed (buildtest.json). This host has no AMX unit (Intel matrix instruction set) and no FPGA (programmable hardware accelerator). So the AMX kernel path and the FPGA path ran only through the test fakes (fake = a stand-in object that replaces the hardware in a test). The only machine runs of real AMX code are the author's runs on delphi-3bda (the Intel Xeon CI machine that has an AMX unit, CI = continuous integration) (the qwen-3-4b model, tp2 = tensor parallel over 2 accelerator cards, 8 users, prompt 1024 tokens, 256 generated tokens, USE_HW_ATTN=0 = CPU attention). The runs are reported in PR comments 5902483127 and 5902523541. testdata-result.json found those runs arithmetically consistent with the code. They were taken from binary bff317e0d3, 33 minutes before the head commit. No FPGA-assisted run exists in this review. /  Words used here: / - forward = one model execution over the scheduled token jobs. / - token job = one token of one user's request scheduled into a forward. / - listener = the object that receives that job's logits (per-word scores). / - decode_like = every token job has a listener. prompt_or_mixed = at least one job lacks one. / - T1..T5 = the five timers, in TSC cycles (the CPU time-stamp counter): T1 forward wall time, T2 attention job time, T3 attention worker 0 job time, T4 period between operations on attention worker 0, T5 join wait. / - pool worker = a thread of the application thread pool, indexed by its pool position. attention workers = the last n_attn_workers pool workers. / - visit = one apply_page_tok call (one query slice against one KV page, a 64-token block of stored keys and values). / - path = which kernel served the visit (empty, avx, amx, fpga). / - FUSE leaf = a file under /model/<id>/attention/ served by the in-process FUSE file system (a user-space file system). / - kill switch = the environment variable TRON_AMX_DISABLE, which makes AMX report unavailable. / - TRON_AMX_DISPATCH = the option of CMake (the build configuration tool) that compiles the AMX kernels (default OFF, CMakeLists.txt:48). / - minibatch = one q_batch, one of the slices a forward's token jobs are split into (q_batch is the code's name for such a slice). / - chunked prefill = a long prompt processed over several forwards, one chunk per forward. / - EAGLE = a small draft model that proposes tokens for the target model. / - MoE = mixture-of-experts models (gpt-oss, mixtral, qwen-3-30b-a3b).
Finding ids (R1-Mn = merged finding n of the first review round, R2-Mn = merged finding n of the second review round) refer to findings-compact.json.

tests.tests_intro: Each row of the test table names one test case or section that the PR adds or touches. It names the production boundary the case calls (a stats hook alone, or a production function such as apply_page_range or run_joins). It says whether a fake (a test substitute for real hardware or a real scheduler) keeps the information the assertion needs. It names the semantic break that would fail the case, and the breaks it does not catch. It gives a verdict. items: Exactly one production entry point exists. state.forward is called only at full.hpp:2090, and run_forward is called only from forward(). So every forward passes through the forward_scope object (the per-forward record holder) [h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2090; h/tron/models/model.hpp:1697; grep of h/, src/, t/].

forward_scope is the first statement after the perfetto slice (perfetto is the tracing library, and a slice is one traced time interval) and before the latch guard (with_latch_arena, the object that marks the forward's latch arena, its pool of synchronization latches, as in use and clears it at the end). So T1 (the forward wall timer) starts after the slice opens. Its destructor runs after with_latch_arena's destructor and before the slice closes. This is what the T1 span of the Note (Note [Attention path stats], the explanatory comment block at the top of attn_stats.hpp) and the single-caller comment describe [model.hpp:1655-1673, 1658-1667, 1706-1711; h/tron/threading.hpp:262-266; h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:30-33, 852-857].

T1 covers logits (per-word scores) and listener delivery. run_logits waits on logits_done per chunk and on listeners_notified before returning. q_batches.clear() (q_batches is the forward's list of minibatches, the slices of token jobs that the plugin runs as a unit) and the arena release both precede the scope destructor [model.hpp:1774, 3317, 3320].

The class (decode_like or prompt_or_mixed) is decided once from in_listener_index.size() == in_token_jobs.size() and stored in current_class. Every per-forward hook reads current_class_ix(). So token_jobs, listener_jobs, kv_only_jobs, fpga_queries, token_jobs_by_path_set, visits, T2-T5 and n_attn_workers min/max all use that forward's class [model.hpp:1668-1672; attn_stats.hpp:453, 471, 484, 492, 508, 517, 526, 534, 542, 565, 593].

forwards and token_jobs move under one object. Both writers sit in ~forward_scope. The raw-hook half record (a record where only one of forwards and token_jobs advanced, reachable only by calling the hooks directly instead of through forward_scope) is documented and tested as a non-production path [attn_stats.hpp:879-883; t/t_attn_stats.cpp:406-430].
The forward_scope destructor is noexcept, and forward() is noexcept. So no exception path leaves a half record [attn_stats.hpp:879-883; model.hpp:1653].

The fold (end_forward's merge of per-worker path bits into per-job path sets) reads only the rows that the attention workers of the current split wrote (the split is forward_n_attn_workers, the number of trailing pool workers that act as attention workers). note_attn_workers runs once per forward and sets forward_n_attn_workers. end_forward folds rows [n_workers - split, n_workers) and clears them. begin_forward resets the split to UNKNOWN_SPLIT, so a forward without attention folds every row [model.hpp:2303; h/tron/plugins/llama.hpp:596; ingest/src/TronCpp.hs:1214; attn_stats.hpp:460, 560-571; t/t_attn_stats.cpp:767-806].

Empty forwards are excluded consistently. full.hpp returns before state.forward and before metrics.forward_passes++. So forwards and forward_passes agree, and forward_scope never receives zero jobs from the scheduler [full.hpp:1999-2005, 2101].

end_forward with zero token jobs and empty fpga_bits passes both asserts. With UNKNOWN_SPLIT the fold reads path_bits[w][job] only in vectors that begin_forward sized. So a plugin that never called note_attn_workers indexes nothing out of range [attn_stats.hpp:455-459, 556-559, 562-573].

With n_layers == 0 and the switch on, rows, fpga and timers are empty vectors, and no code path indexes them. row(), fpga_at() and timers_at() are reached only from hooks the mock plugin never calls [attn_stats.hpp:377-380].

The listener-count equality is exactly "every token job has a listener". One listener is registered per node (a node and an edge are the units of the scheduler's token tree), once per node per forward, always at a token that is a job. Both ensure_listener calls sit inside the frame that pushed the paired job. listener_index names the edge's last token. Edges have at least one token [full.hpp:1157, 2131-2139, 2137, 2364, 2375, 2455-2469; h/tron/scheduler/token_tree.hpp:480-481; model.hpp:1669].

TRON_ASSERT_LE(n_listeners, n_token_jobs) in begin_forward cannot fire through full_scheduler, including the EAGLE child scheduler. Every listener_index entry pairs with a distinct token job, and the vectors are rebuilt per forward [attn_stats.hpp:452; full.hpp:1941-1946, 2455-2469].

Partial-edge chunking never registers a listener without its job: the listener needs processed_tokens == token_count, and the descent stops at the children of a partially processed node [full.hpp:2455, 2933-2934].

A speculative verify step is decode_like for the target model, as the PR body and the forward_counters comment say. speculate.cpp sends one token per draft node with an exact-logits listener. full.cpp registers one listener per call [src/tron/scheduler/speculate.cpp:702-712; src/tron/scheduler/full.cpp:191-192; attn_stats.hpp:52-55, 294; model.hpp:1659-1662; scout-context.txt PRBODY:299].
The class comment's "1-token final prompt chunk" case is correct: such a chunk yields one KV job plus a listener attached to that same job [model.hpp:1661; full.hpp:2457-2459].

A node with a listener whose edge is entirely KV-ready yields a do_kv=0 query-only job with a listener. model.hpp accepts that job. So this forward is decode_like under the rule, consistent with the Note [full.hpp:2461-2468; model.hpp:1814-1815].

The EAGLE draft state is a full_scheduler child with its own state, model and model_stats (is_eagle comes from eagle_cfg.max_layers = 1 through the plugin). It enters through the same full.hpp:2090 site. It publishes under attention_eagle [full.hpp:1767-1777, 2090; src/tron/legacy_dispatch.cpp:73-77; llama.hpp:367; h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:496-499; attn_stats.hpp:919-920; t/t_attn_stats.cpp:903-926].
Every model::state constructs the stats object and its leaves. So no model's leaves are missing, and models that run no attention read zeros [self_attention.hpp:477-500].

assemble_attention_plan runs once per forward on the main thread before the workers are enqueued. So note_attn_workers and the note_fpga_query loop of construct_hw_plan run once per (forward, minibatch). A minibatch is one slice of the forward's token jobs that the plugin runs as a unit. Generated plugins (model plugins emitted by ingest, the repository's code generator in ingest/src/TronCpp.hs) assert one minibatch [TronCpp.hs:1184, 1211-1218, 1235-1238; model.hpp:1759, 2303, 2313, 2747-2755].

n_attn_workers_min renders 0 when no forward of the class ran, so the UINT64_MAX initial value never reaches a reader. Lens 5 cited attn_stats.hpp:816-819 for this render, but my grep at HEAD puts it at 774-777 [attn_stats.hpp:774-778; t/t_attn_stats.cpp:761-765].

Path bits are written at the forward-level token job index tok_ix.i (items[batch_job_ix] is a token_job_id). That is the same index fpga_bits uses and the fold reads. The span is sized for token_jobs.size(). That size equals the forward_scope's count. forward() passes in_token_jobs.size() and then assigns token_jobs = in_token_jobs. token_path_span asserts that size [self_attention.hpp:1487-1489, 1603, 1647, 1652; model.hpp:1668-1672, 1681, 2752; attn_stats.hpp:439-443, 456-458, 566-569].

Path bits cannot leak between forwards. Each end_forward clears the bits it read for jobs [0, n_token_jobs). Rows beyond that range were cleared by the forward that wrote them. begin_forward only grows the vectors and reassigns fpga_bits per forward. end_forward asserts fpga_bits.size() == n_token_jobs [attn_stats.hpp:452, 455, 457, 556, 570].

No stale path bit survives a split change. A worker writes path_bits[pool w][job] only for jobs below n_token_jobs of the forward in which it is an attention worker. end_forward of that same forward clears exactly rows [first_row, n_workers) for those jobs [self_attention.hpp:1487-1489, 1652; attn_stats.hpp:568-571; t/t_attn_stats.cpp:767-806].
The pass index is right: run_sections passes its pending flag and apply_page_range maps it to PASS_PENDING_1 or PASS_READY_0 [self_attention.hpp:1171-1178, 1684].

Pending pages never count under a ready_ key: the page of every do_kv token job goes to pending_page_ixs, and run_sections passes the plan's pending flag to add_visits [model.hpp:1844-1848; self_attention.hpp:1171-1172, 1683-1684].

No visit is double counted across query slices. Every (query, page) pair appears in exactly one section. One apply_page_tok call is one visit. OR-ing the path bit gives the same result however many pages of one token set it [t/t_llama_unit.cpp:2660-2698; self_attention.hpp:1652].

Path values are exhaustive and exclusive: amx comes only from the dense AMX branch with 64 K tokens (one full page of 64 key tokens), empty only when relevant_k_tokens == 0, and avx otherwise with the scored count [self_attention.hpp:1889-1898, 1947-1950, 1982].

Kill-switch identity holds by construction. The dense predicate (begin 0, end 64, one visible range holding token 63, token 0 inside the window) is exactly the condition under which the dotter loop (the AVX loop that scores the K tokens of a page with dot products) scores all 64 tokens. So an AMX-on amx visit is a kill-switch avx_full_page visit. A full page that is not dense is avx_full_page in both arms (an arm is one run configuration, here AMX on or the kill switch). The AVX arm packs nothing. amx_on is false there [self_attention.hpp:1546, 1639, 1726-1728, 1922-1945].

On the kill switch and on AMX-less hosts, available() false makes amx_qp nullptr. apply_page_tok then reports visit_path::avx with the full page. avx_full_page_visits counts it, and the summary reports amx_available false [self_attention.hpp:1546, 1636-1644, 1898; attn_stats.hpp:213-214, 487; t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp kill-switch section].

Full pages written in the current prompt chunk take AVX even with AMX on. is_dense_amx_page tests the page's last token against the first token's range tok_hi, and a fresh page has one range per token [self_attention.hpp:1596-1597, 1727].
k_tokens is counted once per KV head. apply_page_range runs per kv_head, as the README says [self_attention.hpp:1466; README.stats.md:266].
A call that dismissed every page adds nothing: n_visits == 0 makes add_visits return at once, and the early return precedes any tally [attn_stats.hpp:483; self_attention.hpp:1508].
K tokens scored in software are equal in both arms. The kill switch only moves visits from amx to avx with the same relevant_k_tokens [self_attention.hpp:1898, 1982].

T2's window (run_attention_job's attn_elapsed) is unchanged by the PR. The reads keep attn_elapsed's value and its return. record_attention_time sees the same number. The upstream K/V wait stays outside T2. The diff only renamed the final stamp to t_end. The operation_ix overload's elapsed arithmetic around finish_attention_job is untouched [self_attention.hpp:820, 826, 832, 852-855, 860; llama.hpp:775; model.hpp:2138-2155].
The Note's T2 definition names run_attention_job's attn_elapsed explicitly and is exact for both plugins [attn_stats.hpp:33-35].

T5 lies inside T2 in both join modes. run_joins sits between the T2 reads. Both modes accumulate into the same join_wait_cycles, filed once per job.
